facts.raw_span: an 8-month history of radicular pain radiating from her lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
denied any weakness, autonomic symptoms, history of trauma, or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength, normal abduction and adduction
negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography showed neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
most severe at L5, with no denervation
a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
measuring approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and demonstrated peripheral rim enhancement
causing severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs
MR neurography confirmed that the mass arose from the sciatic nerve at the left ischial groove

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a neurofibroma, a type of benign nerve tumor, which is supported by the presence of a cystic mass in the left L5-S1 foraminal zone and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots.

The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could also be consistent with a perineurioma, a rare type of nerve tumor, which is supported by the presence of a cystic mass in the left L5-S1 foraminal zone and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots.

The patient's symptoms of radicular pain and mild hypesthesia in the left L5-S1 dermatome could be consistent with a lumbar disc herniation, which is supported by the presence of negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs.

The patient's symptoms of radicular pain and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots could be consistent with lumbosacral radiculopathy, which is supported by the presence of mild hypesthesia in the left L5-S1 dermatome.

The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a sciatic nerve tumor, which is supported by the presence of a cystic mass in the left L5-S1 foraminal zone and severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs.

The patient's symptoms of radicular pain and mild hypesthesia in the left L5-S1 dermatome could be consistent with a neuropathic pain syndrome, which is supported by the presence of occasional tingling and negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs.

The finding of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone extending along the course of the sciatic nerve into the left ischial groove, with severe foraminal stenosis and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots, is explained by a neurilemmoma.
